content: 1. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate may alter the metabolism of sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid, potentially reducing their effects. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Co-administration of antibiotics with sodium picosulfate may reduce its efficacy by disrupting colonic bacterial flora necessary for its activation. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate can increase the levels or effects of sonidegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Avoid co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, or limit their use to less than 14 days while monitoring for adverse reactions, particularly musculoskeletal effects. 4. Both sorafenib and erythromycin ethylsuccinate can prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are required. 5. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of sparsentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised, though no dosage adjustment is needed. Regularly monitor blood pressure, serum potassium, edema, and kidney function when sparsentan is co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 6. Stiripentol, a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer, can increase erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Consider reducing the dose of P-glycoprotein substrates if adverse reactions occur during co-administration. 7. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases streptomycin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 8. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases sufentanil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to prolonged or severe adverse effects, including fatal respiratory depression. Caution and monitoring are essential. 9. Both sulfamethoxazole and erythromycin ethylsuccinate can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 10. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of suvorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Reduce the starting dose of suvorexant to 5 mg at bedtime when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 11. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases tacrolimus levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases talazoparib levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Co-administration with P-glycoprotein inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to talazoparib. 13. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases tamoxifen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing its conversion to the active metabolite N-desmethyl tamoxifen. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases tamsulosin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary, and dose reduction may be required for drugs predominantly metabolized by CYP3A. 15. Tazemetostat decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 16. Tecovirimat decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer, so monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness during co-administration. 17. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and telavancin can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 18. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases tezacaftor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Adjust the tezacaftor dosage regimen when co-administered with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 19. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases thiamine levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 20. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases tinidazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 21. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases tobramycin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 22. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases tofacitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. No specific dose adjustment is recommended when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, but reduce the tofacitinib dose if co-administered with both moderate CYP3A4 and potent CYP2C19 inhibitors. 23. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases tolvatptan levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases trabectedin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 25. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases tramadol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Dose adjustment may be necessary to avoid serious adverse events, including seizures and serotonin syndrome. 26. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases trazodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 27. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and trimethoprim can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 28. Triptorelin increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 29. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and tropisetron can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 30. Tucatinib increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Consider reducing the dosage of P-glycoprotein substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. 31. Both valbenazine and erythromycin ethylsuccinate can prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 32. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and valoctocogene roxaparvovec may increase the risk of hepatotoxicity. Monitor liver enzymes closely and consider alternative medications if potential drug interactions are identified. 33. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases valsartan levels by inhibiting hepatic uptake transporter OATP1B1. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 34. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases vardenafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Limit the vardenafil dose to 5 mg per 24 hours. 35. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and venlafaxine can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 36. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases vinblastine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 37. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases vincristine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 38. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases vincristine liposomal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 39. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases vinorelbine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 40. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases vitamin K1 (phytonadione) levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 41. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases voclosporin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 42. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and voriconazole can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 43. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases zaleplon levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 44. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases zanubrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Reduce the zanubrutinib dose to 80 mg twice daily when co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 45. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases ziprasidone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 46. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases zolpidem levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 47. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases zonisamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 48. Acetazolamide increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 49. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases aliskiren levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 50. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases alvimopan levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 51. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases ambrisentan levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 52. Amobarbital decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by increasing its elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 53. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases amoxicillin effects due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 54. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases ampicillin effects due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 55. Anastrozole increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 56. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases armodafinil levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 57. Butabarbital decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by increasing its elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 58. Butalbital decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by increasing its elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 59. Clindamycin and erythromycin ethylsuccinate may reduce each other's effects due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 60. Cyclophosphamide increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 61. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases desloratadine levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 62. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases dicloxacillin effects due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 63. Drospirenone increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 64. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases estradiol vaginal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 65. Ethanol decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 66. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases fexofenadine levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 67. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases lansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 68. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases loratadine levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 69. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases methylprednisolone levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 70. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases nafcillin effects due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 71. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases oxacillin effects due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 72. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases penicillin G aqueous effects due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 73. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases penicillin VK effects due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 74. Pentobarbital decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by increasing its elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 75. Phenobarbital decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by increasing its elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 76. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases prednisone levels by decreasing its metabolism, potentially leading to toxic steroid concentrations and altered mental status. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 77. Primidone decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by increasing its elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown.
